title: Express.js REST API Server Best Practices
keyTechniques: Separate routes, controllers, and services into modular files (router -> controller -> service)
Use expressive error handling middleware (err, req, res, next) as the centralized point for formatting API error responses
Wrap asynchronous controller route handlers with async-wrapper utilities or try-catch blocks to forward unhandled rejections to next(err)
Configure standard middleware early: helmet() for security headers, cors() for cross-origin, and express.json() for body parsing
avoid: Do not write monolithic app.js files with all route handlers in a single script
Do not leak internal database stack traces to the client in production error responses
Do not forget to return when sending res.status().json() to prevent headers already sent errors
